title: Maximum in every window of size k
summary: As people walk past a window that fits k of them, report the tallest in view at every moment, dropping anyone who can never be tallest again.
goal: Report the tallest person in view for every window position

mapping.formal: A deque of indices with decreasing values

examples.label: Eight people, k = 3
examples.explanation: One maximum for each of the six window positions.

examples.label: Falling heights
examples.explanation: The tallest is always the one entering first.

ladder.name: Scan every window
ladder.idea: For each window position, look at all k people and take the tallest.

ladder.name: A heap of who is in view
ladder.idea: Keep heights in a max-heap with their positions; before reading the top, discard tops that have left the window.
ladder.insight: Neighbouring windows share k − 1 people, so keeping them in a structure that knows the tallest avoids rescanning.

ladder.name: A line of candidates
ladder.idea: Keep a line of positions with decreasing heights. A newcomer sends home everyone shorter at the back; the front leaves when it slides out of view. The front is always the tallest.
ladder.insight: Anyone shorter than a newcomer who arrived later can never be the tallest again: the newcomer stays in view longer. Dropping them keeps the line sorted.

transfer.problem: For each day, report the highest temperature over the past seven days.
transfer.explanation: It is a maximum over a fixed-size window that slides by one: keep a decreasing line of candidates.

selfCheck: Removes shorter people from the back before adding a newcomer.
Removes the front when it is outside the window.
Starts reporting once the first window is full.
Stores positions, not heights, so leaving is detected.
